1.

The facts as asseverated by the claimant are hereby succinctly recapitulated: A road accident occurred on 11.10.2020 at about 02:14 AM, in front of Jaisalmer House,
Man Singh Road, New Delhi which resulted in registration of FIR No. 78/2020, U/s 279/337/304-A IPC at PS Tilak Marg.

The transgressing or offending vehicle involved in this case was a TSR bearing registration No. DL1RW-6073 which at the relevant time of accident was being driven by respondent no.1 (R-1) Sh. Raj Kishor Shah, was owned by respondent no. 2 (R-2) Sh Kapil Dev and was insured by respondent no. 3 (R- 3) Go Digit General Insurance Ltd .
The accident resulted in the untimely demise of Rohit Singh Rana, son of the claimant.

It was further alleged that no eye witness was found at the spot and at the hospital and therefore the FIR no 78/2020 got registered at PS Tilak Marg u/s 279/337/304-A IPC on the said DD entry.

19.To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
Step 1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balance, which is considered to be the contribution to the dependant family, constitutes the multiplicand.

Step 2 (Ascertaining the multiplier)
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked DAR 194/2021 Page. 15 of 42 Digitally Gajender Singh Vs Raj Kishore Shah & Ors. signed by Arul Varma Arul

19.To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
Step 1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balance, which is considered to be the contribution to the dependant family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Step 2 (Ascertaining the multiplier)
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked DAR 194/2021 Page. 15 of 42 Digitally Gajender Singh Vs Raj Kishore Shah & Ors. signed by Arul Varma Arul
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.

should be one- third (1/3rd) where the number of dependent family members is 2 to 3, one-fourth (1/4th) where the number of dependent family members is 4 to 6, and one-fifth (1/5th) where the number of dependent family members exceeds six 31.Where
the deceased was a bachelor and the claimants are the parents, the deduction follows a different principle.
In regard to bachelors, normally, 50% is deducted as personal and living expenses, because it is assumed that a bachelor would tend to spend more on himself.
